audit.whatIsWrong: The whole Mega-Gnar threat model on this page is GNAR! (R). Wallop, the Mega form of his W, is never mentioned once — and it is a stun on a flat 7 seconds.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Mega Gnar is too enraged to be hyper and instead can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area', cooldown 7 at every rank. GNAR! is 90/60/30. So during a Mega window the stun you will actually eat, repeatedly, is Wallop — roughly one every seven seconds — while his ultimate comes once. Telling a Rumble player to hold Scrap Shield for GNAR! and saying nothing about Wallop points the defensive cooldown at the rarer threat.
audit.corrected: In Mega form the recurring stun is Wallop, flat 7s. GNAR! is the one-off at 90s falling to 30s. Shield the Wallop you can see coming, not just the ult.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text says Hop 'resets on kills and takes 20+ seconds to come back'. The reset-on-kills claim is not in Riot's data, and the ultimate's rank scaling is never given.
audit.why: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 at 475 range. Riot's description mentions only that he bounces off units he lands on; there is no kill reset. GNAR! is 90/60/30 — a third of the cooldown at rank 3, which means the late-game Mega window is a completely different threat from the level-6 one, and the page treats them as the same.
audit.corrected: Hop is 22s at rank 1 down to 12s, with no kill reset. GNAR! falls from 90s to 30s, so respect the Mega all-in far more late than at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] says The Equalizer's 'slow wall denies his hop escape'. It does not block movement — it is a line of damage and a slow, and a dash goes straight over it.
audit.why: Riot's text for The Equalizer: 'Rumble fires off a group of rockets, creating a wall of flames that damages and slows enemies.' There is no pathing terrain. rumble.json carries a 'terrain' derived flag on R, but the description contradicts it, so the description wins. Hop is a leap — it ignores a slow field entirely once it is airborne. Promising a player their ultimate traps a dash gets them killed chasing.
audit.corrected: The Equalizer burns and slows; it does not wall off a dash. Hop goes over it. Use it to punish the ground he has to cross before and after the leap, not to cage him.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block tracks only GNAR! and gives no numbers, and Boomerang Throw's cooldown is never stated despite the early game being entirely about it.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 falling to 10s, at 1100 range against your 600 cone — and catching the boomerang on its return cuts that cooldown, so a Gnar who catches it is on a far shorter clock than one who does not. That is the countable thing in the early lane and it was missing.
audit.corrected: Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1, 1100 range, and its return trip is a second hit he can catch to cut the cooldown. Step to the side of the return.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late text calls Flamespitter a 'multi-tick channel'.
audit.why: Riot's description has Flamespitter dealing damage in a cone for 3 seconds with no channel language. It matters here because the page's advice elsewhere assumes Gnar can interrupt or outlast it; once the cone is down, his hop out is what ends the damage, not any interrupt.
audit.corrected: Flamespitter is a 3-second cone, not a channel. What ends it is him leaving the cone.

edits.after: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 to your 600 and is only 16s at rank 1 — sidestep the return leg so he cannot catch it and cut that cooldown.
edits.before: Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw out-ranges Flamespitter before you have Heat management feel — respect the poke and play for farm.

edits.after: In Mega form the stun that lands over and over is Wallop on a flat 7s, not GNAR! — hold Scrap Shield for the smash you can see winding up.
edits.before: GNAR! launches him at you with a wall stun — have Scrap Shield ready and kite with Electro-Harpoon before he can land the full combo.

edits.before: Drop Equalizer across Gnar's retreat path at Level 6 — the slow wall denies his hop escape and threatens a kill or flash

edits.after: Transform and lead with Wallop's flat-7s stun, saving GNAR! for a wall bounce once your shield is spent
edits.before: Transform to Mega-Gnar when Scrap Shield is on cooldown and hit GNAR! into a wall for the full bounce stun

edits.after: Hop backward in mini form whenever you enter Danger Zone, leaping clear of the cone and wasting the empowered window
edits.before: Kite backward on hop (E) during mini form whenever Rumble enters Danger Zone to waste empowered Flamespitter casts

edits.after: At Levels 1 and 2 mini-Gnar is purely ranged: Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 600 cone, so you cannot answer it without walking into the poke. Last-hit under tower threat and do not spend Electro Harpoon on someone who hops straight back. The boomerang returns to him, so it can hit you twice, and catching it cuts its 16-second cooldown — stand to the side of the return path and he pays full price. Hyper stacks on his attacks and spells for bonus damage and a move-speed burst, so count his hits and step out before the empowered one. The lane is his here: eat as little as possible and wait for Level 3, where a short trade is on if he over-chases.
edits.before: At Level 1 and 2 mini-Gnar is purely ranged and can stack Hyper on you at Boomerang Throw range — you cannot reach him with Flamespitter without walking into extended poke, so focus on last-hitting under tower threat and do not burn Electro-Harpoon on a target who can hop straight back. His Hyper passive deals bonus damage on every third hit and gives him a burst of move speed, so count his autos and back off when he is on his second stack to deny the empowered proc. The lane is his at these levels: absorb as little poke as possible and wait for Level 3 where you can threaten a short trade if he over-chases.

edits.after: By Levels 4-5 the lane becomes genuinely contested. Mini-Gnar still kites with Hop and Boomerang, but Hop is 22 seconds at rank 1 and only reaches 475 — count it, and the moment he commits without it, walk a full Danger Zone Flamespitter across him. When Mega spawns, do not panic-fight, and do not fixate on GNAR!: Wallop is the stun that actually keeps landing, a flat 7 seconds, so save Scrap Shield for the smash and double-harpoon him out of range between them. At Level 6 The Equalizer changes the math — but it burns and slows, it does not wall him in, so lay it on the ground he must cross rather than expecting it to cage a leap.
edits.before: By Levels 4–5 the lane becomes genuinely contested. Mini-Gnar still kites with hop and Boomerang, but his mana costs and hop cooldown mean he cannot be aggressive forever — watch his hop cooldown (it resets on kills and takes 20+ seconds to come back) and punish him with a full Danger Zone Flamespitter the moment he commits without it. When Mega-Gnar spawns, do not panic-fight: hold Scrap Shield and throw a double Electro-Harpoon to slow him out of GNAR! range, or bait the stun into a wall and shield through it. At Level 6 your Equalizer completely changes the math — the slow wall traps him in either form and threatens burst-plus-kill with zero escape if he mispositions near a wall.

edits.after: First item Liandry's Torment tips this firmly your way: the burn stacks across Flamespitter's 3-second cone and makes every Danger Zone trade brutal against mini-Gnar's modest HP pool, while Equalizer wins fights without you ever standing in melee range. Late, his team cannot group through the burn and slow, and you can lay the wall on a Mega commit before the slam resolves. But respect that window properly — GNAR! drops from 90 seconds at rank 1 to 30 at rank 3, so by three points it is up for almost every fight, and Wallop's flat 7-second stun comes far more often than that. A clean wall bounce on your team still swings a fight. In a straight skirmish your items and heat cycling beat his transformation window.
edits.before: First item Liandry's Torment tips the scales firmly in your favor: the percent-HP burn stacks through Flamespitter's multi-tick channel and makes every Danger Zone trade devastating against mini-Gnar's modest HP pool, while your Equalizer becomes a teamfight-winning tool that does not require you to be in melee range at all. In the late game your Equalizer's massive AoE slow means Gnar's team cannot safely group without eating the burn, and if Gnar tries to force a Mega all-in you can drop the wall on top of the fight before he even finishes the slam animation. Respect a fully-stacked Mega GNAR! into a wall — if he gets that off cleanly on your team it can swing a fight — but in a straight 1v1 or skirmish your item advantage and heat cycling beat his transformation window cleanly.

edits.before: He has hop available and Boomerang range advantage; even if you reach him with Flamespitter he hops away before Danger Zone empowerment deals full value.

edits.before: Hop cooldown and his mana pool limit his ability to be continuously aggressive; watch for a misplay to commit a full Danger Zone Flamespitter into his face.

notes: Three real errors fixed. (1) The page's entire Mega-Gnar threat model was GNAR! (R); Wallop — Mega's W, a stun on a flat 7 seconds — was never named, and it is the stun that actually decides those windows. (2) 'Hop resets on kills' is not in Riot's data; Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 at 475 range. (3) wants.you[2] claimed The Equalizer 'denies his hop escape'. Riot's text describes a wall of flames that damages and slows, with no pathing terrain — a leap goes straight over it. rumble.json carries a 'terrain' derived flag on R and on Scrap Shield (W); both contradict Riot's own descriptions and should be treated as tooltip-parse misfires. For the same reason the _missing-interactions entry 'Both sides carry displacement (Scrap Shield (W) vs GNAR! (R))' is wrong — Scrap Shield is a shield plus a move-speed burst with no displacement — and was not written to the page. Left as-is: the existing claim that Hyper procs on every third hit is not spelled out in Riot's text (which says only that attacks and spells hype him up), so I kept the mechanic described in general terms rather than repeating the specific count.
